text:
Recent research favors evaluating individual explanation claims against evidence. [On the Factual Consistency of Text-based Explainable Recommendation Models (2025/2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366) finds high semantic similarity despite poor statement-level factual precision; its review-based supervision is unavailable here, but its claim-level evaluation approach transfers. Proposed adaptation: attach title/description spans or history events to each claim; label support, contradiction, or insufficient evidence. Report direct relevance separately from compatibility. Missing specifications mean “compatibility unknown”; interaction history establishes past interaction, not ownership, satisfaction, or an unmet need.

Overlap also needs separate diagnostics. [Beyond Item Dissimilarities (2024/2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12327) shows benefits from diversifying across intents rather than merely maximizing item dissimilarity. For this task, measure repeated IDs, likely same-product variants, and title/description overlap separately; treat semantic overlap as a redundancy proxy, not proof that recommendations are interchangeable. Infer neither diversity preferences nor hidden user traits. Evidence-backed explanations also need not describe model causality: [Walk the Talk? (2025)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/b5ec50eb177908f21f78ed0d76ed525c-Abstract-Conference.html) evaluates faithfulness through counterfactual interventions.

[Calibrating the Predictions for Top-N Recommendations (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11596) demonstrates that good catalog-wide calibration can conceal poor calibration among recommended items. Proposed adaptation: compare relevance, compatibility-support, and redundancy proxies against the twenty users’ explicit feedback on presented recommendations. Use simple thresholds, leave-one-user-out checks, and user-level uncertainty intervals; twenty users cannot establish reliable category-specific calibration. Abstain on unsupported diagnostic claims and report error versus coverage, while preserving required recommendation output and macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion. Missing feedback remains unknown.
